sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present appeal is filed by the appellant - Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 14.5.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jamnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.76 of 2009, by which, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Rs.2,08,400/- with 9% p.a. interest to be paid to claimant/s, by holding opponents no.2 and 3 liable, jointly and severally.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.76 of 2009
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. The facts of the present appeal are as under :
2.1 The claimant filed the claim petition before the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2804/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined learned Tribunal claiming compensation by stating that on 1.8.2008, he was going on motorcycle Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jagdishbhai Lakhabhai Mungara on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170064371/
1 no.GJ-10P-8495 and his co-villager was a pillion rider thereon; that at about 9.00 p.m., when he reached near Octroi post of Gulabnagar, tractor no.GJ-10-AF-2268 and trailer no.GJ-10Y-1034 came from Rajkot side in full speed, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, and while taking a sharp turn towards Gulabnagar, took in its sweep the motorcycle of the claimant and in this accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
2.2

entities.text: Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jagdishbhai Lakhabhai Mungara
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The notices were served to the opponents.
The opponent nos.1 and 3-insurance companies of both the vehicles appeared and filed their replies.
The issues were framed by the Tribunal.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were led before the Tribunal.
After hearing the submissions made by the rival parties, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition(s) and awarded compensation as noted above.
2.3 Hence, the insurance company of the tractor has filed the present appeal before this Court.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant - Insurance Company has submitted that the present case is a clear case of false implication wherein in the FIR as well as the station NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2804/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined diary, it is categorically stated that the original opponent no.2 himself was driving the vehicle, therefore, there is a case of self-negligence, however, to escape the liability, Pathan Hasanbhai has been projected as a driver; that the liability fastened on the appellant is erroneous, more particularly, in view of the facts and circumstances pertaining to the head on collision between the vehicles involved; that the learned Tribunal has awarded excessive and exorbitant amounts under the heads.
He, therefore, submitted that this appeal be allowed.

4. Per contra, learned advocates for the claimant and the insurance company of the motorcycle, have submitted that the impugned judgment and award is just and proper, which is passed after considering the oral and documentary evidence led before it and the rival submissions submitted before it.
They, therefore, submitted that this appeal be dismissed.
5. I have considered the submissions made by the respective parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
I have also considered the pleadings of the parties before the Tribunal.

5.1 On the point of change of driver's name, the learned Tribunal has discussed that though the name of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2804/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined owner of the tractor and trailer i.e. the opponent no.2 is shown as driver of the said vehicle and based on it, the station diary is written, however, in the further statement, the claimant has clarified that as the opponent no.2 came to see him in the hospital, he gave the name of the opponent no.2 as the driver but in fact, the tractor-trailer was driven by Hasan Sidi Pathan and the chargesheet is also filed against the said Hasanbhai after investigation.

In absence of any contrary evidence to show Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jagdishbhai Lakhabhai Mungara on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170064371/
2 that the said Hasanbhai has approached any forum for his wrongful implication in the offence and filing a false chargesheet against him, the learned Tribunal came to the conclusion that the difference in the name of tractor-trailer driver in the complaint and chargesheet is reasonably explained.

entities.text: Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jagdishbhai Lakhabhai Mungara
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There seems no infirmity to interfere with the said finding of the learned Tribunal on this point.

5.2 On the ground of negligence, it transpires that the learned Tribunal has discussed that it is mentioned in the FIR that the accident occurred while the tractor was taking a turn towards Gulabnagar; that the driver or owner of the tractor has not stepped into the witness box in order to rebut the allegations of negligence made against the tractor driver; the chargesheet is filed against the tractor driver after the investigation and therefore, adverse inference can be NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2804/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined drawn against the driver of the tractor-trailer.

The learned Tribunal has also considered the panchanama of scene of offence and observed that there was head on collision and though it was the duty of the claimant also to drive his motorcycle at moderate speed so that he could stop it on seeing tractor a sharp turn from the opening of the road divider, therefore, considering the facts of the case and the size of the vehicles,
the learned Tribunal held the tractor driver negligent to the extent of 80% and the claimant himself negligent to the extent of 20%.
5.3.

On the point of quantum, the learned Tribunal has assessed the monthly income on the basis of the evidence led before it and calculated the amount of compensation by considering the permanent partial disability occurred by the claimant, applying the multiplier as applicable, the medical expenditure and other expenses incurred by the claimant due to the accident and awarded the amount of compensation, which is just and proper.

It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of `just and fair'
compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of `just compensation' which ought to be NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2804/2018 ORDER DATED:
15/07/2024 undefined determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavour should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
Considering this principle, the amount awarded cannot be considered to be on the higher side.
6. There are catena of decisions that the award of the rate of interest is the discretion of the Tribunal which should be exercised by considering the facts and circumstances of each case.

The provisions of MV Act are benevolent legislation and normally it should be construed that the provisions of the MV Act are enacted to see that the claimants could get some amount of compensation where the claimants either lose their bread earner or has received serious injuries.
There cannot be any perfect arithmetic calculation for awarding amount of calculation.

Therefore, the appeal is required to be dismissed as the learned Tribunal has considered all the aspects and awarded the compensation to the claimant, which is not required to be interfered with in this appeal.

This appeal is, therefore,
required to be dismissed.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2804/2018 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined 7.1
The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.

7.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, pursuant to the order of this Court if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure, within a period of six weeks from today.
7.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
